sn37.3:1.3: An unmarried girl (_kumāribhūta_) under twenty was said to be not mature enough for full ordination ([pli-tv-bi-vb-pc71:1.11]()), which is the same age as for the monks. A _gihigatā_ of just twelve, however, might be ordained. _Gihigatā_ is explained as “gone to the place of a man” (_purisantaragatā_, [pli-tv-bi-vb-pc66:2.7]()); i.e. a girl who is married. This item precedes menstruation, which also suggests the age of twelve. The Hindu tradition says a girl should be given in marriage before puberty (Manu 9.89; Gautama 18.21; Vaśiṣṭha 17.70; Baudhāyana 4.1.11). If no suitable husband is found, three years after puberty she is free to choose her own (Manu 9.90; Gautama 18.20; Baudhāyana 4.10.14). Yama (Vīramitrodaya-Saṃskāra, p. 773) says she may choose a husband after the age of twelve.
